words.meaning: The system of water flowing away from an area.

medium.simple_explanation: The way water naturally flows away from an area through rivers and streams.
medium.funny_explanation: It's basically the Earth's giant plumbing system that prevents your backyard from turning into a permanent swimming pool.

examples.text: The geography teacher explained that the drainage of the region depends on the slope of the land.
The drainage in my garden is so bad that even a tiny rain shower invites all the neighborhood ducks for a party.

words.meaning: Basic parts that make up something.
Relating to the air around the earth.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the layer of air (atmosphere) that surrounds the Earth.
medium.funny_explanation: Anything to do with that giant, invisible air-bubble we all live in that keeps us from floating into space.

examples.text: Scientists study atmospheric pressure to predict if a storm is coming.
The atmospheric conditions in my room are currently 90% dirty sock smell and 10% oxygen.

words.meaning: To exist or be common in a place.

hard.funny_explanation: Like that one catchy song that is playing everywhere you go, whether you want to hear it or not.

words.meaning: Average weather over a very long time.

medium.funny_explanation: When things just can't stay the same—like how your hair looks great in the mirror but looks like a bird's nest in school photos.

examples.text: There are many variations in temperature across the different states of India.

words.meaning: The layer of gases surrounding the earth.
How hot or cold something is.
The force caused by the weight of air.
The amount of water vapor in the air.

medium.funny_explanation: That sticky feeling where the air feels like it's trying to give you a big, sweaty hug that you didn't ask for.

examples.text: High humidity in the coastal regions makes the summer heat feel much worse.
The humidity was so high that my hair expanded into a giant, fluffy cloud the moment I stepped outside.

words.meaning: Rain, snow, or hail that falls to ground.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used as a technical term for all forms of water falling from the sky (rain, snow, etc.).
hard.simple_explanation: Any form of water, like rain or snow, that falls to the ground from the clouds.
hard.funny_explanation: Nature's way of throwing a drink on Earth, sometimes as liquid water and sometimes as frozen ice cubes.

examples.text: The Himalayas receive most of their precipitation in the form of heavy snowfall.
I checked the weather for 'precipitation,' but I didn't expect the sky to dump a whole bucket on my head.

hard.real_world_analogy: A giant celestial sprinkler system that can switch between 'mist', 'shower', and 'ice' modes.

words.meaning: To change frequently from one level to another.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes how weather conditions change frequently and unpredictably within a single day.
hard.simple_explanation: To change or shift back and forth irregularly; to rise and fall.
hard.funny_explanation: Like your phone's battery percentage when you're using a really old charger.

examples.text: Desert temperatures fluctuate wildly, being boiling hot at noon and freezing at night.

words.meaning: A way something is usually done or repeated.

I gave a generalised answer about where my lunch went: 'It has been consumed.'

words.meaning: Large areas or parts of the world.

medium.funny_explanation: Like a word or an idea going on a journey from one place just to end up in your textbook.

Most of my great ideas are derived from things I saw in cartoons while eating cereal.

words.meaning: In the exact or most basic sense.

medium.simple_explanation: Exactly according to the meaning of the words; not exaggerated.
medium.funny_explanation: Using a word to mean exactly what it says, like when you say 'I'm literally starving'—unless you actually are, you're using it wrong!

examples.text: The Arabic word 'mausim' literally translates to 'season' in English.
I was literally the only person at the party who dressed up as a giant taco.

words.meaning: A change to the opposite direction.

medium.funny_explanation: When the wind or your luck does a total U-turn and goes the other way without warning.

There was a complete reversal of roles when the cat started chasing the big dog around the yard.

words.meaning: Explained what something is like.
Able to be seen or noticed clearly.

There was a perceptible silence in the room after I accidentally called the teacher 'Mom'.

hard.real_world_analogy: The difference between a mild spicy sauce and a 'burn-your-tongue' sauce is definitely perceptible.

words.meaning: Belonging to a specific area or district.

Liquid in thermometers used to show temperature.

hard.funny_explanation: A shy metal that hides at the bottom when it's cold but tries to climb out of the tube when it's hot.

I occasionally try to eat a salad, but a burger usually wins the argument.

hard.funny_explanation: When the weather acts like a dramatic teenager because the ocean isn't nearby to keep it calm, switching between 'oven mode' and 'freezer mode'.

words.meaning: Physical features of a land surface.

The relief of my backyard is mostly just one giant hole where the dog tried to find treasure.

words.meaning: The degree to which something is curved.

The curvature of a banana makes it the perfect natural telephone for pretending to call monkeys.

words.meaning: Imaginary line dividing Earth into north and south.

medium.funny_explanation: Like a backpack so stuffed with old papers that you can't even fit a stick of gum inside.

The fog was so dense this morning that I almost accidentally tried to walk the neighbor's cat.

words.meaning: The power to have an effect on something.
Making something less extreme or intense.

hard.simple_explanation: Making something less extreme, intense, or violent.
hard.funny_explanation: Acting like the sensible friend who stops you from making a scene when you're super angry or super excited.

examples.text: The sea exerts a moderating influence on the climate of coastal cities like Mumbai.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a thermostat that automatically turns on the fan when it gets too warm and the heater when it gets too cold.

words.meaning: To put forth or use power or influence.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes how the sea applies or brings its influence onto the land's climate.
hard.simple_explanation: To apply or bring to bear a force, influence, or quality.
hard.funny_explanation: Using effort to make something happen, like how you exert your brain power to solve a puzzle while your cat exerts its power to sit on your keyboard.

My alarm clock exerts a great deal of effort to wake me up, but I exert more effort in hitting snooze.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a principal walking into a noisy classroom; their mere presence exerts a quietening force on the students.

words.meaning: Moving from the sea toward the land.

medium.simple_explanation: Moving from the sea towards the land.
medium.funny_explanation: Winds that are finished with their ocean swim and are heading to the beach for a snack.

examples.text: Onshore winds can bring moisture and cooler air to coastal cities.
The onshore wind was so strong it blew my ice cream cone right back into the ocean.

The subtropics are perfect for people who like the sun but don't want to live inside a giant steam-room.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like the porch of a house; it’s not inside the heated room (Tropics), but it’s still much warmer than the front gate (Poles).

words.meaning: Deciding or settling a result or outcome.

hard.funny_explanation: When the clouds get too heavy and decide to drop everything they're holding right on your head.

I checked the forecast for precipitation and ended up looking like a drowned rat five minutes later.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a leaky faucet in the sky that sometimes drips (drizzle) and sometimes breaks entirely (downpour).

words.meaning: The side of something facing away from wind.

hard.funny_explanation: The 'Safe Zone' behind a mountain where the wind can't find you to blow your hat off.

words.meaning: Features or qualities that identify something.

words.meaning: The height of a place above sea level.

Calling India just a country is like calling a triple-decker burger just a snack—it's practically a subcontinent of food.

medium.funny_explanation: A piece of land that's too big to be just a country but didn't quite make it to full continent status.
